main_text.l: pellat,& tandem in illas erumpit voces?
[tainè monstro me amicum posse fieri
calumniator putet? ego admiratione
prodigioque calumniæ perculsus, hæs-
ito, quid oporteat respondere, meque in
mille mortes condemno, si vel suspitio
talis de me uspiam fuerit. Imò tantum
abest, ab Imperatore vel armis impet-
endo, vel lancinando lingua aut cala-
mo; ut passim per eandem Apologiam,
se pro eius incolumitate tum priuatim,
tum publicè preces fudisse fateatur: ni-
hil aliud dixi, quàm precamur pro salu-
te Reliogiosissimi Imperatoris Constan-
tij,& statim uniuersus populus una voce
acclamauit, Christe auxiliare Constantio,
& magna perseuerantia has preces
continuauit. ] Sed interim alij per Chri-
stianum Orbem Episcopi centū & 16. à
suis sedibus ex Imperatoris Edicto pulsi,
quid meditantur? quid moliuntur?
quid Iulius Pontifex Romanus ab Ar-
rianis excommunicatus? quid Liberius
amandatus in exilium (legatis suis in
carcerem conjectis? ) cur non suum
fulmen in Imperatoris caput ejacula-
tur? imò audi ipsius fulmen in Epistola ad

page.notes: Line 1 begins mid-sentence, so the paragraph continues from the previous page. "Reliogiosissimi" is printed that way (probably for Religiosissimi) and is left as printed. Uncertain: the opening bracket "[tainè" and the reading "tainè". The single paragraph runs to the catchword; no paragraph break is visible. The bracket "]" after "continuauit." is printed as shown. Italic spans: "Constantij," "Christe auxiliare Constantio," "Iulius," "Liberius".
